See [common behavior](common.md) for owned-value conventions and inherited methods.

An Edit owns a candidate based on a document version. Read through edit.meshes to see its writes. A normal with-block exit commits and waits; an exceptional exit cancels. Explicit commit() returns a Job that must be waited for.

Ordinary write failures abort the candidate even when caught. Repair the input and create a new Edit. OutcomeUnknown requires recovery of the original call. See the [recovery guide](../guide.md).

## zipzi.Edit

**Type**

`(factory-owned; use the documented public entry)`

One mutable candidate owned by one sequential caller. Use session.edit. Successful writes advance sequence; publication is a separate Job and ordinary failures cannot be caught into a successful commit. Reads through this Edit include its pending writes. Normal context exit commits and waits; an exceptional exit cancels ordinary candidates. Recover unknown calls before cleanup.

A closed/aborted/unknown Edit is rejected. Normal scope exit commits and
waits; an explicit cancel is the other successful exit state.


## zipzi.Edit.__exit__

**Callable**

`(kind: object, exception: BaseException | None, traceback: object) -> None`

Confirm commit/cancel on normal exit, never turn an unknown into success.

Python supplies the context arguments. Normal exit accepts only a
confirmed committed or explicitly cancelled state; it may commit and
wait synchronously. Caught ordinary write failures raise EDIT_ABORTED.
Caught unknown outcomes raise their recoverable original exception again.
An already propagating exception is preserved; ordinary candidates are
cancelled, accepted work may be waited, and cleanup failures become notes.
No unknown write is replayed or silently aborted. Returns None.
